description: Create paths with integer values and retrieve values only for paths that have been created. A new path is valid only when its immediate parent already exists. Example 1: create /a with value 1, then /a/b with value 2; both values can be read. Example 2: attempting /c/d before /c exists fails, then creating /c allows it to be read. Constraints: paths begin with /, contain lowercase components, and are not the root path.
intuition: A path trie lets each creation verify that its parent node exists before inserting the final component.

brute_force.approach: Store full path strings and check for a parent path in a set before each insertion.
brute_force.time: createPath O(path length), get O(1) average

optimal.approach: Store each path component in a trie, locating the parent and final node in one traversal.
optimal.time: createPath O(path length), get O(path length)

edge_cases: A path cannot be created twice.
A child cannot be created before its direct parent.
